pk.context: 40 mg single oral dose, healthy adults

pill.desc: opaque capsule with a green cap and an orange body (40 mg)

clues.title: Approval
clues.text: Approved by FDA in December 1987. Now supplied only as capsules, in 10, 20 and 40 mg strengths.

clues.title: Sponsor
clues.text: Held by Eli Lilly. The label names its Dista Products division as the marketer.

clues.title: Class
clues.text: A selective serotonin reuptake inhibitor. The exact mechanism is unknown but presumed to be inhibition of neuronal serotonin uptake in the CNS.

clues.title: Enantiomers
clues.text: A 50/50 racemate. Both enantiomers are potent, specific serotonin uptake inhibitors with essentially equivalent pharmacologic activity.

clues.title: Drug substance
clues.text: A hydrochloride salt of molecular weight 345.79; the free base is C₁₇H₁₈F₃NO. White to off-white crystalline solid, 14 mg/mL soluble in water.

clues.title: Capsule
clues.text: Opaque capsules with a green cap. The body is green at 10 mg, yellow at 20 mg and orange at 40 mg.

clues.title: Absorption
clues.text: After a single 40 mg dose, plasma peaks of 15 to 55 ng/mL arrive 6 to 8 hours later. Food may delay absorption by 1 to 2 hours; 94.5% is protein bound.

clues.title: Elimination
clues.text: Half-life is 1 to 3 days after one dose and 4 to 6 days on chronic dosing. The active demethylated metabolite lasts 4 to 16 days, so steady state is slow to reach and to leave.

clues.title: Boxed warning
clues.text: Boxed warning: antidepressants increased suicidal thoughts and behavior in children, adolescents and young adults in short-term studies.

clues.title: Indications
clues.text: Indicated for major depressive disorder, OCD, bulimia nervosa and panic disorder; with olanzapine, for bipolar I depression and treatment-resistant depression.
